questions.title: The F₂ genotype ratio
questions.text: The genotype of a green-stemmed tomato plant is GG and that of a purple-stemmed tomato plant is gg. The hybrid of a cross between these two was self-pollinated to obtain F₂ progeny. What will be the ratio of GG, Gg and gg in this F₂ progeny?
steps: ① GG × gg ⟹ F₁ all Gg
② Self F₁: Gg × Gg
③ Gametes: G, g from each parent
④ Square: GG, Gg, Gg, gg
questions.remember: Monohybrid F₂: genotype ratio 1 : 2 : 1; phenotype ratio 3 : 1 (dominant : recessive).
questions.trap: Picking 3 : 1 : 0 by mixing up the PHENOTYPE ratio (3 : 1) with the genotype ratio.
questions.tryit: What fraction of the F₂ plants have purple stems?

questions.title: New combinations in a dihybrid cross
questions.text:
Two pea plants, one with round green seeds (RRyy) and another with wrinkled yellow seeds (rrYY), were crossed, producing F₁ progeny with only round yellow (RrYy) seeds. When F₁ plants are self-pollinated, the F₂ progeny will have which new combinations of characters, as compared to the parents?
(i) Round, yellow  (ii) Round, green  (iii) Wrinkled, yellow  (iv) Wrinkled, green
steps: ① Parents: round GREEN and wrinkled YELLOW
② F₂ shows all four: round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow, wrinkled green
③ Round green and wrinkled yellow = the parents' looks ✗
④ Round yellow and wrinkled green are NEW ✓
∴ (i) and (iv) → (b)
questions.remember: In a dihybrid cross, traits are inherited independently, so F₂ shows new combinations not present in either parent (9 : 3 : 3 : 1).
questions.trap: Picking (ii) and (iii): those are exactly the PARENTS' combinations, not new ones.
questions.tryit: In a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio, how many of 16 are wrinkled green?

questions.title: An egg meets a Y sperm
questions.text: When a human egg is fertilised by a sperm having a Y chromosome, the zygote has the following combination of chromosomes:
steps: ① Egg: 22 + X
② Sperm with Y: 22 + Y
③ Zygote: 44 + XY
④ XY ⟹ a boy
questions.remember: Humans: 23 pairs = 22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes. Eggs always carry X; sperm carry X or Y, so the father's sperm decides the sex.
questions.trap: Picking 22 + XY: a zygote has the FULL set, 44 autosomes, not 22.
questions.tryit: What does a sperm carrying X produce with an egg?

questions.title: Traits you can't inherit
questions.text:
Identify the traits that cannot be transmitted from parents to the offspring:
(i) Swimming technique  (ii) Blood group  (iii) Eye colour  (iv) Dancing skills
steps: ① Inherited traits are controlled by genes in DNA
② Blood group and eye colour: genes ✓ inherited
③ Swimming and dancing are LEARNT during life
④ Acquired traits don't change DNA ⟹ not passed on
∴ (i) and (iv) → (b)
questions.remember: Inherited traits come from genes (blood group, eye colour, ear lobes). Acquired traits are learnt or developed in life (skills, muscles, a cut tail) and are not inherited.
questions.trap: Thinking a champion swimmer's child is born knowing how to swim. Skills are acquired, not in the DNA.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 8 · Section 8.2 (inherited vs acquired traits)
questions.tryit: Is a scar from an injury passed on to children?

questions.title: Red and white pea flowers: 33 : 11
questions.text:
A pea plant with red flowers was crossed with a pea plant with white flowers. 30 F₁ seeds were sown: all plants bore red flowers. 44 F₂ seeds were sown: 33 plants bore red flowers and 11 bore white flowers.
(a) Depict the information in the form of a cross.
(b) Deduce the F₂ phenotypic ratio and genotypic ratio.
steps: ① All F₁ red ⟹ red is dominant (R), white recessive (r)
② Parents RR × rr ⟹ F₁ all Rr (red)
③ F₁ selfed: Rr × Rr
④ F₂: RR, Rr, Rr, rr
⑤ Phenotype 3 red : 1 white (33 : 11 = 3 : 1)
⑥ Genotype 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr
questions.ans: RR × rr → F₁ all Rr (red); Rr × Rr → F₂ 3 red : 1 white (phenotype), 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr (genotype)
questions.remember: If all F₁ show one trait, that trait is dominant. Convert actual numbers to the ratio: 33 : 11 = 3 : 1.
questions.trap: Writing only the numbers 33 : 11. The marking scheme wants the RATIO 3 : 1 and the genotypes 1 : 2 : 1.
questions.tryit: Out of the 33 red F₂ plants, about how many are pure breeding (RR)?

questions.title: Sex determination: genes or not?
questions.text:
(a) Giving two examples, justify the statement that the sex of the offspring in all animals is not always genetically determined.
(b) Differentiate between the sex chromosomes of male and female human beings.
steps: ① (a) Some reptiles: the temperature at which eggs are kept decides the sex
② Some snails can change sex during life
③ So sex isn't always decided by genes
④ (b) Female: XX, a perfect pair
⑤ Male: XY, a mismatched pair (Y is shorter)
∴ Temperature, snails · XX vs XY
questions.ans: (a) In some reptiles, egg temperature decides the sex; some snails can change sex · (b) females have a perfect pair XX; males have a mismatched pair XY (Y shorter)
questions.remember: In humans sex is genetically determined: the sperm (X or Y) decides; chances of a boy or girl are 50 : 50.
questions.trap: (a): giving human examples. The question asks for animals where sex is NOT decided by genes.
questions.tryit: Who decides the sex of a human child: the mother or the father?
questions.tryans: The father (his sperm carries X or Y)

questions.title: Tall purple × short white: to F₂
questions.text:
For pea plants: tall T (dominant), short t (recessive); purple flowers P (dominant), white p (recessive).
(a) Cross a pure plant dominant for both traits with a plant recessive for both traits, and work out the progeny up to F₂.
(b) What is the probability of obtaining tall plants with white flowers in F₂?
steps: ① Parents: TTPP (tall purple) × ttpp (short white)
② F₁: all TtPp, tall purple
③ F₁ gametes: TP, Tp, tP, tp
④ 16 boxes: 9 tall purple, 3 tall white, 3 short purple, 1 short white
⑤ Tall white = 3 of 16
∴ 9 : 3 : 3 : 1; probability 3/16
questions.ans: TTPP × ttpp → F₁ TtPp (tall purple); F₂ 9 tall purple : 3 tall white : 3 short purple : 1 short white; P(tall white) = 3/16
questions.remember: Dihybrid F₂ is always 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, with both dominant traits in 9, one dominant in each 3, both recessive in 1.
questions.trap: Writing 1/16 for tall white. 1/16 is SHORT white (both recessive); tall white (one dominant) is 3/16.
questions.tryit: What is the probability of a short plant with purple flowers in F₂?
